Dolores Hidalgo is closely associated with the beginning of Mexico's struggle for independence. It was here that the priest Miguel Hidalgo called for an uprising against Spanish rule. The city's history makes it an important stop on routes through central Mexico.

Today, visitors continue their exploration along streets lined with colonial architecture, markets and artisan workshops. Locally made goods and everyday town life sit alongside historic landmarks. Dolores Hidalgo is often visited together with Guanajuato, combining the story of independence with walks through Mexico's old towns.

Drake Bay is located on Costa Rica's southern Pacific coast, where the shoreline meets tropical rainforest. The area is known for nature excursions: boats depart from the coast for parts of Corcovado and nearby islands.

The bay itself offers beaches, coastal vegetation and ocean views. Boat journeys reveal the coastline from another perspective, while forest walks complement the time spent at sea. Drake Bay makes a convenient base for travelers spending several days exploring the nature of southern Costa Rica and enjoying a peaceful stay by the water.

The Drake Passage separates South America from the Antarctic Peninsula. This ocean passage, approximately 850 km wide, connects the southeastern Pacific Ocean with the southwestern Atlantic. The Antarctic Circumpolar Current flows through it, linking the waters around the continent.

For passengers aboard expedition ships, crossing the Drake Passage is the sea leg of their journey to Antarctica. From the deck, travelers watch the ocean and seabirds, while weather determines the conditions of the crossing. The passage is included in the Antarctica section of the catalog as part of an itinerary through international ocean waters. This classification describes the geography of the journey, not national sovereignty.

### Georgetown, Guyana's Garden City!

Georgetown is known as the Garden City of the Caribbean. Its clearly laid-out rectangular grid of streets is decorated with greenery from gardens and parks. The thoughtful layout makes the streets easy to navigate. Among the city's principal cultural and historical landmarks are the world's largest wooden Anglican cathedral, built in 1892, and a Catholic cathedral constructed from reinforced concrete panels.

After admiring the architecture, visitors can head to Georgetown's zoo to discover its exceptionally rich wildlife, or see sea turtles laying their eggs at Shell Beach during the season. The long Seawall sea defense and a network of canals and sluices built by the Dutch protect the city from flooding. Local residents have long made these engineering structures a popular recreation area, with numerous places for swimming and sunbathing.

## A Dream Trip to Waterfalls and Mountains

### Tours Around Georgetown!

Mount Roraima, a vast plateau standing at around 3,000 meters above sea level and wrapped in clouds, leaves a lasting impression on visitors. The powerful torrents of Kaieteur Falls plunge over a 226-meter rock ledge into a mist-filled abyss. Countless droplets create a brilliant rainbow around this spectacular waterfall, one of the most beautiful and powerful on the planet, located in western Guyana.

Eduardo Avaroa National Reserve is part of high-altitude itineraries following a crossing of the Uyuni Salt Flat. The route passes through the volcanic landscapes of the Lípez region.

During the journey, travelers visit lagoons, observe Andean flamingos and explore desert landscapes. The exact stops depend on the chosen route through southwestern Bolivia.
